verdict.rationale: Microsoft's Entra documentation confirms the Authenticator app stores device-bound passkeys and signs users in with them using biometrics or a PIN, based on WebAuthn standards. However, that documentation covers organizational (Entra) sign-in, and nothing in the pack shows an everyday user saving passkeys for arbitrary third-party websites and apps. missing for 10: evidence of passkey storage and sign-in for personal or third-party websites and apps, consumer-facing passkey setup docs, independent or hands-on corroboration of passkey sign-in.

support.subject: As an everyday user, the app stores passkeys and signs me into websites and apps with them, not just TOTP codes

citations.quote: Users can sign in with a passkey in the Authenticator app and complete phishing-resistant authentication with their biometric sign-in or device PIN.
Passkeys in the Authenticator app are device-bound to ensure that they never leave the device they were created on.
Users stay up-to-date with latest passkey innovation based upon open WebAuthn standards.
